title: Steam Trap

introduction.definition: A steam trap is an automatic valve that discharges condensate and air from steam systems while preventing live steam from escaping. In the inverted bucket trap, steam under the bucket makes it float and close the valve; when condensate fills the bucket and the trapped steam escapes through the vent hole, the bucket sinks, opens the valve and system pressure pushes the condensate out.
applications: Turbine and plant steam systems (alumina digestion, evaporation)
key_points: Mechanical (bucket, float), thermostatic and thermodynamic families
Failed-open traps waste energy; failed-closed traps waterlog equipment
Regular trap surveys pay back quickly
introduction.summary: A steam trap automatically drains condensate (and air) from steam lines and equipment while holding back live steam. In the inverted bucket trap, steam entering under the bucket makes it float and close the valve; when condensate fills the bucket and the steam escapes through the small vent hole, the bucket sinks, opens the valve and condensate is pushed out — an intermittent cycle.

foundation: Support the valve and adjoining pipe so the body does not carry pipe weight or thermal loads; heavy valves need their own supports.
alignment: Align flanges face-to-face and bore-to-bore before bolting; never pull pipes into place with the bolts.
Respect the flow-direction arrow on the body.
piping: Install below the drain point with a strainer and isolation valves; provide a test/sight point.
Prime (fill) inverted bucket traps before start-up.
commissioning: Check the valve strokes fully and smoothly.
Pressure-test the line (shell test) with the valve partly open; do not use the valve to blind a test above its seat rating.
Record the as-installed position and set points.

symptoms: Live steam at outlet, high return temperature

remedies: Restore trap function, proper drip legs

video_tutorials.title: Steam Trap — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Steam Trap.
A steam trap is an automatic valve that discharges condensate and air from steam systems while preventing live steam from escaping.

In the inverted bucket trap, steam under the bucket makes it float and close the valve; when condensate fills the bucket and the trapped steam escapes through the vent hole, the bucket sinks, opens the valve and system pressure pushes the condensate out.
Typical applications include steam main drip legs; heat exchangers, reboilers and coils; steam tracing; turbine and plant steam systems (alumina digestion, evaporation).
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Trap Body, Cap, Inlet Riser & Valve Seat.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Steam Trap works.
Condensate from the steam line enters through the inlet riser.
Steam entering under the bucket makes it buoyant — the bucket rises.
The lever presses the valve head onto the seat — no steam escapes.
Steam condenses / vents through the bucket hole; condensate fills the bucket and it sinks.
The valve opens and condensate is pushed out to the return line.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

video_tutorials.title: Steam Trap — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Steam Trap.
Survey traps with ultrasound/temperature.
Clean strainer.
Replace valve and seat mechanism.
Watch for blowing steam (failed open): live steam at outlet, high return temperature. Common cause: lost water seal, worn seat.
Watch for blocked (failed closed): cold trap, waterlogged equipment. Common cause: dirt, closed vent.
Watch for water hammer: banging in steam lines. Common cause: condensate not drained.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
